frames.subtitle: Meet Sarah. She's a travel agent at a mid-market TMC managing 32 corporate customers. Until now, she's been living in legacy booking tools."
This is her Engine dashboard. Everything she manages—
every customer...
every policy, every report—lives in one place.
Let's say Acme Corp's travel manager just texted. Their VP is booking a flight tomorrow and needs a special rate approved.
Sarah easily switches to that account...
Engine remembers her context. She's now inside Acme's account—their policies, their rates, their travelers. Completely isolated from her other 31 customers.
Acme's policy recently changed. They now allow business class on flights over 6 hours, but only for directors and above.
Sarah updates that rule in less than ten seconds. When a policy changes, it saves for every related traveler without lifting a finger.
Okay. Acme's VP finally submitted that travel request. Sarah receives it in Engine
Engine knows Acme's policy, their negotiated rates, their preferred carriers. The options are already filtered and ranked for her.
No digging through policies. No hunting across supplier sites.
Sarah books in seconds instead of minutes.
It can be one booking or dozens. It's that easy.
As the month ends, Sarah pulls her commission report. Engine tracks every booking, every policy save, every negotiated rate across all her customers.
She can drill down by customer...
...by travel type...
...by policy. And because Engine connects directly to the GDS, the numbers are real-time...
One platform. 32 customers. Zero context switching.
Engine. Built for how TMCs actually work.
